author: Rahul kp
title: Forfeiture &
simple_words: Company cancels shares when a call is unpaid, keeps the money received, and later sells the shares again.

definitions.meaning: Cancelling a defaulting member's shares for non-payment of a call, as per Articles. The amount already received is not refunded.
definitions.note: Share capital is debited at called-up amount

definitions.meaning: Selling the forfeited shares again, often as fully paid, at par or at a discount. Discount cannot exceed the forfeited amount on those shares.

key_points: On forfeiture, debit ==Share Capital== at the !!called-up amount!!, not the face value.
Credit ==Forfeited Shares A/c== with the amount actually received; credit Calls in Arrear for the unpaid part.
Premium already received stays in Securities Premium A/c. If premium was !!not received!!, debit Securities Premium too.
After reissue, the gain on those shares is transferred to ==Capital Reserve==.

formulas.name: Capital Reserve on reissue
formulas.legend: F = amount forfeited on the shares reissued (received amount); D = discount allowed on reissue of those shares.

entries.label: On forfeiture
entries.narration: Being shares forfeited; premium debited only if unpaid

entries.label: On reissue at a discount
entries.narration: Being forfeited shares reissued as fully paid at a discount

entries.label: Gain on reissued shares
entries.narration: Being gain on reissued shares transferred to Capital Reserve

insight.text: Only the Forfeited Shares balance of the reissued shares, after discount, becomes Capital Reserve.

memory_trick.explanation: Money received stays in Forfeited Shares A/c; unpaid amount goes out through Calls in Arrear. Reissue surplus then moves to Capital Reserve.

exam_tip: In MCQs, profit on forfeiture and reissue goes to Capital Reserve, never to the Profit and Loss account.

doubt.question: Is the whole Forfeited Shares balance Capital Reserve?
doubt.answer: No. Only the part for the shares reissued, after discount, is transferred. Balance for unissued shares stays in Forfeited Shares A/c.

mistakes.wrong: Debiting Share Capital at face value on forfeiture
mistakes.right: Debit Share Capital at the amount actually called up on the forfeited shares.

mistakes.wrong: Transferring the full Forfeited Shares balance to Capital Reserve after a part reissue
mistakes.right: Transfer only the amount relating to the shares reissued, less discount allowed.

mistakes.wrong: Crediting profit on reissue to Profit and Loss A/c
mistakes.right: Credit the gain to Capital Reserve A/c.

reviewer_note: Key point 3 corrected: premium received stays in Securities Premium A/c; premium unpaid is debited. Check P10-1-24 wording for the past-paper point.
check_notes: Writer: Key point 3 corrected: premium received stays in Securities Premium A/c; premium unpaid is debited. Check P10-1-24 wording for the past-paper point.

Checker 1: Key point 2 and formula 1 legend: 'amount actually received' / '(received amount)' should say 'amount received towards share capital (excluding any securities premium received)'. Premium already received stays in Securities Premium A/c and is not credited to Forfeited Shares A/c. Suggested wording: 'Credit Forfeited Shares A/c with the amount received on share capital (excluding premium).'

Checker 1: Journal entry 1 / key point 2 (wording only): the unpaid amount can be credited either to Calls in Arrear A/c or directly to the unpaid Allotment/Call A/c. Add 'or respective unpaid call A/c' so both accepted methods are covered.
Checker 1: Definition 2 (wording only): shares can also be reissued at a premium. Better wording: 'at par, at a premium or at a discount'.
